study type: Cross-sectional study (retrospective analysis of surveillance data)
exposure: dieting during the year before pregnancy
cohort: The study included 51,399 women who participated in PRAMS phase 7, had a prepregnancy body mass index >=25 kg/m2, and a singleton birth.
finding: Prepregnancy dieting was associated with lower odds of SGA but higher odds of excessive gestational weight gain, gestational diabetes, and LGA infants, with excessive GWG mediating the association between prepregnancy dieting and LGA.
cross-section timing: Data was analyzed from the PRAMS surveillance project, which collects data on maternal health before, during, and after pregnancy, with outcomes measured during pregnancy or at birth.
